newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SOCCER-CHRISTMAS CHEER FOR HUNGARIAN FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHRISTMAS CHEER FOR HUNGARIAN FANS.

text.p: Hungary's success-starved football fans have received a surprise Christmas present courtesy of the BBC and the English Football Association.

Forty-three years after their football team defeated England 6-3 at Wembley Stadium in what has been called "the game of the century," Hungarian fans will at last have a chance to see the whole game on television after the BBC donated a cassette to the cash-strapped Hungarian State Television (MTV).@

The game, in November 1953, was the first time England had been beaten at Wembley and introduced the world to stars such as Ferenc Puskas and Nandor Hidegkuti. Yet, ironically, the Hungarians never saw their greatest moment.

At the time there was no television in Hungary and fans had to rely on radio for information on the action. A few days after the game 20 minutes of highlights were shown in cinemas across the country.
The programme will be shown on Christmas Day.

"We wanted to evoke a heroic moment in British-Hungarian sporting history. The fact that it has never been shown before, gives a special resonance here," Britain's ambassador to Hungary, Christopher Long, said.
Hungarian fans have had little to cheer of late, as their national team have failed to qualify for any major international tournament in over a decade.
